To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
genetic variation in epigenetic genes may moderate emotional reactivity to daily life events.

1) three SNPs of DNMA3A (rs1465764,rs1465825,rs11683424) and one SNP of MTHF (rs1801133) moderated the impact of stress on negative affect in daily life, 2) these effects were replicated in a population based sample, 3) the direction of the effect was consistent across 5 samples, 4) the effect of rs11683424 was also significant in patients with a psychotic disorder
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of epigenetic genes in the development of emotional reactivity.
the interplay between epigenetic mechanisms and environmental influences on emotional reactivity.
epigenetic mechanisms and how they mediate the impact environmental influences on the development of mental disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence for epistatic interactions between epigenetic genes and daily stressors on emotional reactivity in healthy subjects.
epigenetic genes do not seem to be involved in the regulation of emotional responses to pleasant and stressful stimuli as assessed by the ESM.
epigenetic-regulating genes do not play a major role in stress-induced emotional changes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the epigenetic genes DNMT3A and MTHFR are associated with emotional reactivity to stressful events, but not to pleasant events.
the DNMT3A gene is involved in the epige-netic machinery and that genetic variations in this gene are associated with the emotional response to stress in daily life.

the genetic variation in epigenetic genes may be a potential risk factor for the development of psychiatric disorders, and the epigenetic genes are involved in the regulation of the emotion and the emotion regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genetic variants involved in epigenetic regulation do not seem to have a major impact on emotional reactivity to daily life events.
genetic variants in genes involved in epigenetic mechanisms do not have a direct effect on affective responses, but may moderate the impact of daily life stressors.

the epigenetic genes DNMT3A and MTHFR may moderate the effect of stressful daily life events on negative affect, but that the effect sizes are relatively small and that further research is needed to replicate and extend our findings.
